incidentPremise: A maintenance crew sealed a basement plant room after reporting 'cold that moves'. Two of the three came back. The site has been without mains power for six days and the anomaly has spread as far as the stairwell.
_engineNote: This file is now read by a generic engine: src/sim/anomaly.js switches on nothing this anomaly is called. `presence.field` says how it disturbs the scalar field, each trigger names a `sense` from the closed vocabulary in src/sim/senses.js, and each capability names a `verb` from the same file. A JSON key may name a QUANTITY, never an OPERATOR (GDD 20.6).

field._note: It is a cold mass, so it SUBTRACTS from the heat field. This is why a fence that was exactly good enough on the way in is not good enough at contact: the thing you are fencing is actively lowering the wall.

perception.recordingInterference: None. It is invisible to the eye and to cameras in the visible spectrum, but thermal imaging and frost traces record it faithfully. Deliberately consistent: an anomaly that also corrupted recordings would give players no reliable channel at all.
accessibilityAlternatives: The thermal imager announces contact with a distinct rising tone as well as the visual gradient, so the presence cue does not require reading a colour ramp.
Frost traces carry a shape tell (radial cracking) in addition to colour, readable without fine colour discrimination.

states.description: Settled in the coldest reachable volume. Does not move. Leaves a slowly growing frost bloom.

presentation.visualTell: Frost bloom on the nearest metal surface, radial cracking pattern
presentation.environmentalTell: Ambient temperature falls by roughly one degree per minute within the room

states.description: Has registered a heat source and begins drifting toward it at walking pace. Still avoidable.

presentation.visualTell: Frost trail extends along the floor toward the heat source
presentation.audioCue: Draught acquires direction and a faint whistle
presentation.environmentalTell: Loose paper and dust move against the building's airflow

states.description: Locked onto the strongest heat source in range and closing. Contact causes rapid heat loss and mobility injury.

presentation.visualTell: Continuous frost path, breath fogs heavily
presentation.audioCue: Whistle sharpens to a sustained note
presentation.environmentalTell: Standing water skins over with ice

states.description: Held against a heat gradient it cannot cross. Stationary and enclosable for as long as the gradient holds.

presentation.visualTell: Frost edge stops dead in a straight line at the heat boundary
presentation.environmentalTell: Temperature on the warm side stops falling

states.description: Sealed inside an insulated transit case with its internal heater cycling. Custody established.

presentation.visualTell: Case exterior frosts at the seams under load
presentation.audioCue: Heater cycling audibly, roughly every twenty seconds

triggers.condition: any player or powered heat source within 12m for longer than 4s
triggers.telegraph: The steady draught acquires direction and the frost bloom elongates toward the source before any movement begins.

triggers.condition: strongest heat source within 6m and unobstructed by a thermal barrier
triggers.telegraph: Whistle sharpens for roughly two seconds before the drift accelerates.

triggers.condition: a continuous heat gradient above 40C spans the anomaly's approach path
triggers.telegraph: Frost edge halts visibly at the gradient before the state settles.

triggers.condition: heat gradient falls below 40C or is breached for longer than 3s
triggers.telegraph: Flutter returns to a sustained note; frost resumes crossing the old boundary.

triggers.condition: insulated transit case closed around the anomaly with heater active
triggers.telegraph: Case seams frost as load transfers.

capabilities.effect: Rapid heat loss on contact: exposure condition plus mobility injury. Survivable once; compounding on repeat.
Battery-powered equipment within range loses charge at roughly four times the normal rate.
Freezes standing water into a slip hazard that persists after the anomaly moves on.

constraints.description: Cannot cross a sustained heat gradient above 40C. This is the whole procedure: the squad does not fight it, they fence it.
Cannot pass through closed-cell insulation. Portable barrier panels work; sheet metal and plasterboard do not.
Moves at roughly half pace where airflow is dead. Killing the ventilation buys the team time and is a legitimate alternative to spending heaters.
Always visible on thermal imaging regardless of state. There is no stealth phase; the difficulty is coverage, not detection.

_evidenceNote:
GDD §27.2 asks for at least two evidence paths per required rule. This file shipped with exactly one each, which meant a squad that walked past a single pickup could never learn that rule at all — not found it harder, could not. The five entries added at revision 0.5.0 are second paths, not second copies, and the list is now read in PAIRS: each rule's two entries sit together, and each pair is two different kinds of observation.

The reliabilities inside a pair are deliberately mismatched. §7.3 grades an observation confirmed, probable or disputed, and two confirmed sources for one rule is one source written twice. A squad holding the frost bloom AND the chart recorder knows something a squad holding two frost blooms does not: that a second, weaker channel agrees. The heat-wall pair is the sharpest case — a frost edge you can put a hand across, and a hypothermic man in an ambulance saying the same four words eleven times with his core at 31.4C.

`thermal-visibility` is the one rule whose first path costs cargo, so its second path is the dead crew's own imager, lying on the floor with its review buffer still full. It teaches the rule without granting live coverage, which is exactly the distinction the loadout wager is made of.

⚠ AND TWO PATHS PER ANOMALY IS THE WRONG DENOMINATOR, which is what revision 0.6.0 is about. A squad does not play an anomaly, it plays an incident package, and a package places only the subset of these entries that makes sense on its floor. `ashlar-gallery-draught` placed seven of the twelve, because the other five are cold-store fiction — a chart recorder on a plant wall, two lamps in an aisle, a charging rack in the bay — and none of those things exists in a condemned crosswall block. So five of these rules had exactly ONE path on the floor a squad was standing on while the per-anomaly count read a clean 25 of 25.

The five added at 0.6.0 — `hot-works-permit`, `tubular-heaters`, `accident-book`, `fire-watch-camera`, `alarm-cells` — are ASHLAR's second paths, and the fix was to author them rather than to move the cold store's. They are all the same building's paperwork and plant: a permit book, a fire point, an accident book, frost heaters on a tank room wall, a temporary alarm running off cells. Nothing was relocated, because relocating a chart recorder into a stripped-out flat would have been a lie that passed the test. Each rule is therefore read as a TRIPLE now — one entry the cold store places, one the gallery places, and one either shared or earned — and the reliabilities still disagree inside each set.

evidenceRules.rawObservation: Radial frost cracking on a metal surface, growing measurably over two minutes, with no condensation source nearby.

Cold-store chart recorder on the plant wall, seven-day paper, still turning on its clockwork. The trace holds flat at -18 until Tuesday, then falls off the bottom of the chart four separate times. Each of the four begins within two minutes of an entry on the door card hung beside it, and none of them begins with the floor empty.

Hot-works permit book on the bench in the plant store, carbons still in it. Five permits raised for burning brackets off the ninth floor, and all five signed off after the fire-watch hour. On four of them the watchman has written the same thing in the box where his initials go — CAME OVER COLD, PACKED UP. The fifth is scored through, torch never lit, and its box is empty.
Surviving crew member states it 'came for the warm one first' and that the man carrying the lamp was taken.

Two lamps lie eleven metres apart in the same aisle, both flat now: a floodlight head on a stand, and a hand torch on the floor. The frost path runs the full eleven metres, passes the torch within a hand's width without turning, and ends in a bloom that has lifted the paint off the floodlight's housing.

Three tubular frost heaters run along the tank room wall, warm to the back of the hand, still fed off the contractor's temporaries. The fitters' fan heater lies five metres past them on its side, casing split, element white with frost. The track through eleven months of screed dust runs the length of the room, passes under the tubulars without turning, and ends at the fan heater.
Frost stops in a straight line two metres from a still-warm boiler, and does not resume on the far side.

Ambulance handover sheet for the second crew member, taken on the way out. He answers no question that is put to him and says 'stay by the pipes' eleven times. The medic has written a core temperature of 31.4C against it, and 'not orientated to place'.

Accident book out of the first-aid tin in Flat 4, where the crew took their breaks. One entry for the ninth floor: cold burn to the back of the left hand, fractured left wrist, treated at the Royal, off since. The description is in the injured fitter's own block capitals, written with the wrong hand — BEHIND THE LAMPS. REACHED OUT PAST THEM. The supervisor has put 'not witnessed' underneath it and countersigned that.
Thermal imager shows a coherent sub-ambient mass roughly 1.5m across holding its shape while it moves.

The crew's own thermal imager, face down on the floor with eleven percent of its cell left. The review buffer holds ninety seconds: a sub-ambient mass crosses the frame twice, once against the racking and once against open floor, and its outline measures the same across on both passes.

The thermal camera off the fire point in the drying room, signed out for the hour after every burn and back on its charger since. Its card holds fourteen stills. Eleven are brackets cooling. Three were taken eight minutes apart on the same night and are the same sub-ambient shape three times: once in a doorway against the crosswall, once in open corridor, once low against the gallery's north face. It measures the same across in all three.
Two separate battery-powered tools lost charge four times faster than rated while in the same room.
A four-way charging rack in the bay, dead with the rest of the floor. All four packs on it show zero on their own gauges. Two identical packs still boxed underneath it, never fitted, show full.

Wireless call point at the head of the west stair, part of the contractor's temporary fire alarm, every device on it running off its own cell. Its fault lamp is lit and the cell behind the cover is flat. So are the other two on this floor. The spares taped inside each cover, same box and same date code, all read full.
Plant room log records the chiller running continuously for eleven days before the incident, against a four-hour duty cycle.
Sustained cold draught in the stairwell moving against the building's designed airflow.

_claimsNote:
The hypothesis board, and it is content now. It was seven claims frozen into src/sim/evidence.js and every incident got them, so the lodger's board asserted that a 40C gradient stops a thing that has never been recorded moving. This set is the draught's own board, unchanged in wording, id and order from the array it replaces — src/sim/evidence.js keeps that array as the fallback for a definition that ships no board, and section AP asserts the two have not drifted.

Read in the same SETS the evidence list is read in: every entry that reveals a rule sits on the one claim about that rule, so a squad holding any two of them has a claim that can go strong — whichever floor it found them on. That is the property the suite asserts, not 'the claim names one of the sources': a claim citing one source of a set and reaching strong on unrelated ones is a claim that goes green while the rule it is about is still half unlearned. The two false claims each hang off one false lead and neither can go strong, which is what makes them leads rather than a second right answer.

claims.text: It moves toward the strongest heat it can reach.
A sustained heat gradient above 40C stops it dead.
Closed-cell insulation stops it. Steel racking does not.
Thermal imaging sees it in every state. There is no stealth phase.
It drains battery-powered equipment near it.
The failed chiller is the anchor. Kill the chiller and it disperses.
It travels on the building airflow and follows the ductwork.

containment.goal: The anomaly sealed inside an insulated transit case with its heater cycling, verified by a stable case interior temperature for 30 seconds and no frost propagation beyond the seams.

abortConditions: Heater output falls below the gradient threshold with the anomaly inside the fence
Any operative takes a second chill-contact
Ventilation restarts and the anomaly reaches walking pace before the fence is complete
Power pack drops below the reserve needed to hold the gradient through the seal
Thermal coverage of the approach path is lost for longer than 5s
Frost sample compromised before the case is sealed
Any condition from the safe procedure

integrityConditions.failureSignal: Heater cycle audibly lengthens, then frost creeps outward from the case seams.
Floodlight tripods dim in sequence as the pack sheds load; the frost edge starts advancing again.
Thermal feed drops to static on one lane, and the operator loses the mass mid-approach.
